extra_quotes: Phase-contrast microscopy was performed using a Crystalline Tester CP1 (Ceramic Forum Co., Ltd., Japan) equipped with a 20× CFI Plan Fluor DLL positive -phase-contrast objective lens (NA = 0.5, PH1; Nikon, Japan), a ring-aperture condenser (NA = 0.78), and a 405-nm LED light source.
Reflection XRT images of the ammonothermal GaN wafer were acquired using six equivalent g = 11−24 reflections at BL3C of the High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK).
The dislocation was characterized by weak-beam dark -field imaging and large-angle convergent -beam electron diffraction (LACBED) analysis to determine its Burgers vector26–30.

When the inclination of a threading edge dislocation with respect to the optical axis becomes large, linear contrast arising from the inclined dislocation line is superimposed on the dipole -like contrast, making determination of the Burgers vector difficult.
